Dairy Products and Equipment Sectional Committee, FAD 57

NATIONAL FOREWORD This Indian Standard, which is identical with IS0 4099 : 1984 `Cheese - Determination of nitrate and nitrite contents - Method by cadmium reduction and photometry', issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendation of the Dairy Products and Equipment Sectional Committee and approval of the Food and Agriculture Division Council. This standard was first published in 1981, based on IS0 4099 : 1978. With the revision of corresponding IS0 standard, this standard is also being revised to align it with latest IS0 standard. This revision incorporates, among others, the following major changes: a) Procedure in relation to checking the reducing capacity of the reduction column, extraction and deproteination has been modified. b) Formula for calculation of nitrite content has been modified. c) Precision of the test, specified in terms of reproducibility and repeatability has been incorporated. d) Precise dimensions have been incorporated in the figure of apparatus for nitrate reduction. In the adopted standard certain terminology and conventions are not identical with those used in the Indian Standards; attention is particularly drawn to the following: a) b) Wherever;the words `International Standard' appear, referring to this standard, they should be read as `Indian Standard'. Comma ( , ) has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian Standards, the current practice is to use a point ( ) as the decimal marker.

In this Indian Standard, the following International Standard is referred to. Read in its respective place the following:
international Standard Corresponding Indian Standard

IS0 707 : 1985 Milk and milk products of sampling

Methods

IS 11546 : 1985 Methods of sampling of milk and milk products ( Identical )

In reporting the result of a test or ayalysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be reounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised)`.

Indian Standard OF NITRATE AND CHEESE - DETERMINATION NITRITE CONTENTS - METHOD BY CADMIUM REDUCTION AND PHOTOMETRY ( First Revision )

1

Scope

and field

of application

5

Reagents

This International Standard specifies a method by cadmium reduction and photometry for the determination of the nitrate and nitrite contents of cheese.

All reagents shall be of recognized analytical grade. The water used shall be distilled or deionized water, free from nitrate and nitrite.
NOTE - In order to avoid possible inclusion of small gas bubbles in the copperized cadmium column (6.10), the distilled or deionized water used for the preparation of the column B.l), for checking the reducing capacity of the column (8.21, and for regeneration of the column (8.3) should preferably be freshly boiled and afterwards cooled to room temperature.

The method is suitable for hard, semi-hard and soft cheeses of various ages and for processed cheese.
The detection limits

of the method

are

5 mg

of

nitrate

per

kilogram

and 0,5

mg of nitrite

per kilogram.

8.4

Preparation

of the test sample

the copperized

Prior to analysis, remove the rind or mouldy surface layer of the cheese, in such a way as to obtain a sample representative of the cheese as it is usually consumed. Grind the sample by means of an appropriate device; mix the ground mass quickly, and, if possible, grind it a second time and again mix thoroughly. sample kneading. Transfer the test sample to an airtight container until the time to Clean the device after grinding each sample. If the be ground, mix it thoroughly by intensive cannot

Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standardsare also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards : Monthly Additions'.
